subject: On‑prem infra validation & worker/storage plan for Aurora Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@aurorahealth.org>, infra@aurorahealth.org
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem infra validation & worker/storage plan for Aurora Health

Hi Alice / Aurora infra team,

Thanks for the kickoff call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together an initial checklist and the validation items we need to complete before we schedule the rack walkthrough. Items we want to validate on site or via your infra diagrams: 

- Control plane topology: preferred 3 control-plane VMs (HA) with external etcd or stacked etcd? Please share current HCI/VM design or metal controller plan.
- Worker pools (we use the term worker pools rather than nodepools internally): expected workload mix (inference, API-serving, batch retraining jobs). Rough estimate: API-serving (low latency) vs batch (high throughput).
- Network/IP plan: management network ranges, pod CIDR(s), service CIDR, existing VLANs, MTU, and whether BGP-based routing is available.
- Egress/NAT and firewall: outbound egress rules (do you NAT at the site edge?), ports we must open (6443, 30000-32767 if using NodePort, or ALB/ingress ports), and any proxy/transparent TLS interceptors.
- Storage: preferred backend(s) (Ceph/Rook, NFS, SAN/iSCSI). SSD/NVMe available for local ephemeral (KV cache, model cache) vs persistent volumes (longer retention). Typical asks: PV throughput, IOPS requirements for the model-serving pods, snapshot/backup cadence.
- CSI and drivers: which CSI drivers are allowed in the cluster (rook-ceph, csi-nfs, open-iscsi, aws-ebs is irrelevant on-prem).
- Security/compliance hooks: SOC2 evidence we will need (audit logs, KMS usage, network diagrams).

Attachments: I attached a short template for cluster sizing we commonly use (proposed-cluster-sizing.xlsx). Please populate the estimated QPS, model token throughput, and expected concurrency for the API-serving instances. Also send any existing network diagrams and a small inventory of available rack/network appliances.

Deliverables from Aurora (ordered by priority):
1) Network diagram showing VLANs, edge NAT, and intent for pod/service CIDRs.
2) Current storage topology (controller model, RAID configuration, LUN sizes if SAN).
3) A list of IP blocks we can use and any reserved ranges.

Next steps: if you can share diagrams by EOD Tuesday (PST), Marissa will run a sizing pass and we’ll return recommended worker/ssd tiers and a short on‑site checklist. Happy to set a follow up 30min to walk through the spreadsheet.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
[attachment: proposed-cluster-sizing.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@aurorahealth.org>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@aurorahealth.org, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@aurorahealth.org>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem infra validation & worker/storage plan for Aurora Health

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear checklist. Attaching our current network diagram and a short inventory. A few constraints up front:

- We run a three‑zone non‑cloud datacenter footprint (N+1 network fabric). Primary uplinks use BGP to the edge routers; we can announce additional pod CIDRs if needed but prefer not to change the main DC CIDR.
- Storage: Dell Unity SAN presented as LUNs over iSCSI to a pair of storage controllers. We also have two NVMe arrays (local) available for cache/ephemeral.
- Security: SOC2 workstream is active; we must ensure audit logging is forwarded to our SIEM and private keys are stored in our HSM.

I've attached: aurora-network-diagram-v1.png and our quick SOC evidence checklist. Can you confirm whether Redwood requires privileged CSI drivers or elevated cluster-admin for initial installs? We prefer to limit privileged components unless strictly necessary.

On worker pools: our initial ask is to support a POC with two model sizes concurrently (small/medium), plus a canary API lane. If you can propose a minimal worker pool split for POC that keeps latency under 120ms P50, that helps our planning.

Alice
Alice Nguyen
Cloud Infrastructure Lead, Aurora Health
alice.nguyen@aurorahealth.org

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem infra validation & worker/storage plan for Aurora Health (sizing pass)

Ben / team — I reviewed Aurora's diagram and the SAN/NVMe inventory. Below are recommendations I propose we send back as the Redwood POV (keeps the POC lean but production‑portable):

1) Control plane: 3 control-plane VMs on dedicated management VLAN, stacked etcd OK for POC but recommend external etcd for production if Aurora wants controller separation. Use kubeadm with control-plane anti-affinity.

2) Worker pools (proposed):
   - api-serve: 4 x m-3 (16 vCPU, 120GB RAM, 1 x 2TB NVMe) — low latency, enable kube-burst and prefer local NVMe for model cache.
   - inference-gpu (if you plan GPU inference later): label gpu=true; capacity planning only for POC.
   - batch-worker: 2 x c-2 (8 vCPU, 60GB RAM, 1 x 1TB SSD) with taints for batch jobs.
   - infra-storage: 3 x s-1 (8 vCPU, 32GB RAM) to run the Rook/Ceph OSDs if you choose ceph; otherwise attach iSCSI LUNs to the storage-class nodes.

3) Storage strategy:
   - Short term POC: use iSCSI LUNs presented from Unity SAN as a persistent backend with a csi-isci driver and volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer. This avoids standing up Ceph for POC.
   - Medium term: recommend a converged Ceph cluster (Rook) located on the infra-storage pool for higher throughput and better snapshot support.
   - Local NVMe on api-serve nodes for KV cache (redis/model-cache): ephemeral, mounted as hostPath/LocalPV for deterministic IOPS.

4) CSI/privileges: to install the CSI drivers we require cluster-admin during install; we can drop elevated privileges after deploy. Document this in the deployment runbook.

5) Networking: use Calico in policy-only mode if Aurora prefers BGP for route advertisement; set MTU to 9000 on the fabric if supported. Recommend a dedicated pod CIDR per rack to simplify topology-aware volume scheduling.

6) Compliance: we will forward audit logs to your SIEM using Fluentd (TLS to syslog endpoint). Keywrap with your HSM; Redwood will not retain HSM keys.

I attached a quick sizing sheet with node profiles and rough cost/throughput estimates. If you agree, Ben can send this as the consolidated plan and propose dates for the rack walkthrough and an install window.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@aurorahealth.org>, infra@aurorahealth.org
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem infra validation & worker/storage plan for Aurora Health (consolidated plan & next steps)

Alice / team — thanks for the diagram and checklist. Based on Aurora's constraints and Marissa's sizing pass, here's the consolidated plan and immediate asks so we can lock a 2‑day on‑site window the week of Sep 6: 

Consolidated plan (POC):
- Control plane: 3 x HA control-plane VMs (stacked etcd for POC).
- Worker pools: api-serve (4x m-3), batch-worker (2x c-2), infra-storage (3x s-1).
- Storage: use existing Unity SAN LUNs via csi-iscsi for POC; map a pair of NVMe drives per api-serve node for model cache (LocalPV).
- Networking: pod CIDR(s) assigned per rack; we will not modify DC CIDR. MTU 9000 if fabric supports jumbo frames. Calico in policy-only mode + BGP peering at edge for advertised pod ranges.
- Security: audit logs shipped to your SIEM, HSM for KMS, and limited cluster-admin window for CSI installs.

Immediate asks (Aurora):
1) Confirm CIDR pools we can use for pods/services (we need exact /16 or /18 blocks).
2) Confirm which NVMe bays we can allocate as LocalPV on the api‑serve nodes.
3) Confirm a preferred 2‑day on‑site window (we suggested Sep 6 or Sep 13).

Action items & owners:
- Provide final network diagram with explicit CIDRs — Aurora (Alice) — due 2026-08-24
- Validate LUN sizes and presentable iSCSI targets — Aurora (Tom) — due 2026-08-25
- Schedule 2‑day rack walkthrough & install window — Ben/Marissa — target week of Sep 6
- Create JIRA ticket for install tasks and firewall exceptions — Jonas — INFRA-8421

Please let us know if any of the above needs to change. If you confirm dates and deliverables, we’ll prepare the install runbook and an initial Ansible playbook for the bootstrap.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
